result_text:
I fixed the four default conventions in `ScopingConventions.java` so they match the files they were meant for. The new test and the existing `CodeConfigurationTest` pass (6 and 4 tests, no failures).

Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **HTML pages (pkgdown, Doxygen, meta generator):** the path pattern was `(html|html|xhtml)`, which listed `html` twice and left out `htm`. It is now `(html|htm|xhtml)`.
- **.NET documentation XML:** the path pattern `.*/[.]xml` required a literal `/.xml` file. It is now `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches.
- **JavaScript `// Generated by …`:** the path pattern `.*/[.]js` had the same problem. It is now `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches.
- **Gradle JavaScript scripts:** the path pattern `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` required a literal `.-gradle.js`. It is now `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

Content patterns are unchanged, so hand-written `.htm`, `.js` and `.xml` files still don't match the generated rules. The existing matches for `.html`, `.xhtml` and `build.gradle` are preserved.

I also added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks the positive cases above, the existing `.html`/`.xhtml` cases, the negative cases for hand-written files, and `build-gradle.js`. I did not run it against the unfixed code to confirm it fails there.

Nothing is committed.
